Let

\[
p(\lambda)=\prod_{j=1}^4(1-\alpha_j\lambda).
\]

Since \(\sum \alpha_j=2\), every admissible polynomial has

\[
p(0)=1,\qquad p'(0)=-2,
\]

so write

\[
p(x)=1-2x+ax^2+bx^3+cx^4.
\]

The middle active pattern is the decisive one. In that regime the equioscillation points are

\[
u,\ 2,\ v,\ 6
\]

with signs

\[
p(u)=-C,\quad p(2)=C,\quad p(v)=-C,\quad p(6)=C,
\]

and \(u,v\) are interior critical points. Solving these equations gives

\[
C=\frac1{17},
\]

\[
p_0(x)=1-2x+\frac{379}{306}x^2-\frac5{18}x^3+\frac{25}{1224}x^4.
\]

Its derivative factors as

\[
p_0'(x)=\frac{(5x-17)(5x^2-34x+36)}{306}.
\]

Thus the relevant critical points are

\[
u=\frac{17-\sqrt{109}}5,\qquad v=\frac{17+\sqrt{109}}5.
\]

Also

\[
p_0(x)+\frac1{17}
=\frac{(5x^2-34x+36)^2}{1224},
\]

so \(p_0(u)=p_0(v)=-1/17\), and

\[
p_0(x)-\frac1{17}
=\frac{(x-2)(x-6)(25x^2-140x+96)}{1224}.
\]

The extra root in the gap is

\[
x=\frac{24}{5}.
\]

Hence \(p_0(\gamma)\le 1/17\) precisely once \(\gamma\ge 24/5\), and the interior right minimum remains in the interval precisely while

\[
\gamma<\frac{17+\sqrt{109}}5.
\]

Therefore the active sets are:

\[
\frac92<\gamma<\frac{24}{5}:
\qquad
\mathcal A_\gamma=\{u_\gamma,\gamma,v_\gamma,6\},
\]

with signs \(-,+,-,+\).

\[
\frac{24}{5}<\gamma<\frac{17+\sqrt{109}}5:
\qquad
\mathcal A_\gamma=
\left\{
\frac{17-\sqrt{109}}5,\ 2,\ \frac{17+\sqrt{109}}5,\ 6
\right\}.
\]

\[
\frac{17+\sqrt{109}}5<\gamma<\frac{11}{2}:
\qquad
\mathcal A_\gamma=\{u_\gamma,2,\gamma,6\},
\]

again with signs \(-,+,-,+\).

At the first transition,

\[
\gamma=\frac{24}{5},
\]

the active set is

\[
\left\{
\frac{17-\sqrt{109}}5,\ 2,\ \frac{24}{5},\ \frac{17+\sqrt{109}}5,\ 6
\right\}.
\]

At the second transition,

\[
\gamma=\frac{17+\sqrt{109}}5,
\]

the right interior minimum becomes the moving endpoint.

Thus the requested pair is

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{24}{5},\frac{17+\sqrt{109}}5\right)}.
\]
